content:
We have carbon NMR data: chemical shifts: 161.40, 143.85, 130.30, 26.65, 22.80, 21.35, 19.20 ppm.

We need number of CH3 groups in the sample's compound. Methyl carbons appear around 10-30 ppm (aliphatic). Here we have four signals in that region: 26.65, 22.80, 21.35, 19.20. Likely each corresponds to a CH3 carbon. Could be also CH2 or quaternary but typical CH3 ~ 10-30. So likely 4 methyl groups.

But need confirm if any could be CH2. However we have no other data. The aromatic/unsaturated carbons are 161.40, 143.85, 130.30 (likely aromatic or carbonyl). So the low-field signals are aliphatic. Usually CH2 appears ~20-40 as well, but CH3 is more upfield ~10-30. CH2 often ~20-50. Hard to differentiate. But we have four low-field signals; could be mixture of CH3 and CH2. The question: "How many CH3 groups in the sample's compound? If not, reply '0'." We need integer.

We could try to get proton NMR to see methyl singlets. But we don't have SMILES. Could retrieve proton shifts ranges? Not helpful.

Maybe we can get HSQC to map carbon-proton correlation to identify methyls. Use hsqc_nmr_spectra tool (no args).
